picks.excerpt: Judge Araceli Martinez-Olguin granted final approval to the landmark $1.5 billion settlement over Anthropic's use of pirated books to train its models. Roughly 500,000 titles were downloaded illegally; 92% of eligible authors and publishers opted in, at about $3,000 per infringed work.
picks.rationale: The largest copyright class action in US history is now final — it fixes a going rate ($3,000 per work) and a destroy-the-dataset condition that every publisher will negotiate against.

picks.excerpt: Bloomsbury has secured roughly $18.7m (£14m) from the Anthropic copyright settlement, one of the first concrete figures showing what an individual trade publisher recovers when its catalogue is used as AI training data.
picks.rationale: First hard number on what a single trade house actually recovers — turns the abstract settlement into a benchmark publishers can price their own catalogue against.

picks.excerpt: Substack rolled out AI-detection labelling powered by Pangram so readers can see whether a post was AI-assisted — but writers can switch the badge off entirely, making disclosure effectively opt-in.
picks.rationale: A live platform-level AI disclosure system writers can toggle today — the opt-out design decides how much an AI label actually tells a reader.

picks.excerpt: Wiley is the only scientific publisher inside the US Department of Energy's Genesis Mission Consortium, joining Nvidia, AWS, Microsoft, IBM and AMD to supply peer-reviewed content for 'AI-accelerated innovation and discovery'.
picks.rationale: The licensing counter-move to the lawsuits: a major publisher feeding peer-reviewed content straight into a state-backed AI program — a template other houses will copy.

picks.excerpt: Generative AI was the biggest topic across panels at the International Publishers Congress in Kuala Lumpur, from licensing books as training data to how houses restructure editorial and production work around AI.
picks.rationale: Global read on where the trade actually stands — training-data licensing and editorial restructuring ran through every panel at the industry's biggest congress.
